name: Lower-back (lumbar) strain
hint: Hurts when bending, lifting or carrying
description: Acute or recovering strain of the lumbar muscles.
guidance: Avoid axial loading and loaded spinal flexion/rotation; favour supported and spine-neutral work.

contraindications.reason: Axial (spinal compressive) loading aggravates lumbar strain.
Heavy spinal loading should be avoided until pain-free.
Hip-hinge shear forces stress the injured lumbar tissue.
Loaded spinal flexion increases lumbar strain.
Loaded rotation through the lumbar spine is a common aggravator.
Holding a loaded hinged torso demands high lumbar extensor effort.
Long-lever anti-extension loads the lumbar spine heavily.

name: Shoulder impingement
hint: Pinches when lifting your arm up
description: Pain when raising the arm, typically subacromial impingement.
guidance: Avoid overhead pressing and internally rotated elevation; prefer landmine/angled pressing below shoulder height.

contraindications.reason: Overhead positions narrow the subacromial space.
Behind-the-neck positions combine abduction and external rotation at end range.
Loaded internal rotation with elevation (upright row) is a classic impingement position.
Movement places the shoulder in the impingement arc under load.
Full overhead hanging loads the irritated shoulder at end range.

name: Rotator cuff tendinopathy
hint: Deep ache in the shoulder, worse at night or at end range
description: Overuse irritation of the rotator cuff tendons.
guidance: Avoid end-range and overhead loading; keep pressing and pulling in mid-range.

contraindications.reason: Overhead loading compresses the irritated cuff tendons.
Deep shoulder extension (dips) stresses the anterior cuff.
Loaded end-range stretch (deep flyes) strains the cuff.
End-range external rotation under load.

name: Patellar tendinopathy (jumper's knee)
hint: Pain just below the kneecap when squatting or jumping
description: Load-related pain at the patellar tendon below the kneecap.
guidance: Avoid deep knee flexion under load and plyometrics; isometrics (wall sit, Spanish squat) are usually tolerated.

contraindications.reason: Deep knee flexion under load spikes patellar tendon stress.
Jumping and landing are the highest patellar tendon loads.
Knee-forward shear positions overload the tendon.
Heavy open-chain extension loads the tendon near full flexion.

name: Ankle sprain (lateral)
hint: Rolled ankle, still sore or wobbly
description: Recovering inversion sprain of the lateral ankle ligaments.
guidance: Avoid impact and unstable single-leg balance under load; seated, supported and low-impact work is fine.

contraindications.reason: Impact loading risks re-injury of healing ligaments.
Landing mechanics stress the sprained ankle.
Loaded single-leg balance on an unstable ankle risks re-inversion.
Repetitive bouncing on the forefoot.

name: Hamstring strain
hint: Pulled hamstring, tight when stretching or sprinting
description: Grade I–II strain of the hamstring muscle group.
guidance: Avoid loaded lengthening and explosive hip extension early on; bridges and supported hip extension are usually tolerated.

contraindications.reason: Loading the hamstring in a lengthened position can re-tear healing fibres.
Maximal eccentric hamstring load is too high for an acute strain.
Explosive/ballistic movements create sudden hamstring tension.

name: Lateral epicondylalgia (tennis elbow)
hint: Pain on the outside of the elbow when gripping
description: Pain at the outside of the elbow from wrist-extensor overload.
guidance: Avoid heavy gripping and loaded wrist extension; neutral-grip and machine work is preferred.

contraindications.reason: Sustained heavy gripping loads the common extensor tendon.
Loaded wrist extension directly stresses the lateral epicondyle.

name: Wrist sprain
hint: Hurts to bend the wrist back or lean on your hands
description: Sprain of the wrist ligaments, painful in extension and weight bearing.
guidance: Avoid weight bearing through an extended wrist; use handles, straps, or machines.

contraindications.reason: Body weight through an extended wrist stresses the sprained ligaments.
Loaded wrist extension aggravates the sprain.
Loaded wrist flexion under resistance.

name: Neck (cervical) strain
guidance: Avoid loads through the head/neck and heavy shrugging; keep the neck neutral.

contraindications.reason: Direct load or pulling through the cervical spine.
Forces the neck into forward flexion under load.

name: Hip impingement (FAI)
hint: Pinching in the front of the hip when you go deep
description: Femoroacetabular impingement — pinching in deep hip flexion.
guidance: Avoid loaded deep hip flexion; limit squat depth and prefer hip-extension-dominant work.

contraindications.reason: Loaded deep hip flexion pinches the femoral neck against the acetabulum.

name: Groin (adductor) strain
description: Strain of the hip adductor group.
guidance: Avoid heavy adductor loading early; progress gradually.

contraindications.reason: Long-lever adductor isometrics are too demanding early after a strain.
Direct resisted adduction loads the strained tissue.

name: Finger pulley strain (climbers)
hint: Sore finger from climbing or crimping
description: A2/A4 pulley strain — only crimp-grip loading is contraindicated, which no gym exercise in this catalog uses.
guidance: Avoid crimp-grip hangs; ordinary gym training is generally unaffected.

contraindications.reason: Crimp grip loads the finger pulleys maximally.
